title: Few-Shot Prompting: Teaching by Examples
introduction: In this lesson you will learn how to show an AI model examples of the desired answer before asking it to solve a new problem. Using examples can make the model’s responses more reliable and consistent.

sections.heading: Understanding Prompting
sections.subheading: How we give instructions to AI
paragraphs: Prompting is the way we talk to a language model. We write a short text that tells the model what we want it to do.
A good prompt is clear, concise, and matches the task we need.

example.title: Simple summary request
example.content: Prompt: "Summarize the following paragraph: The sun rises in the east and sets in the west."

sections.heading: Zero-Shot Prompting
paragraphs: Zero-shot prompting means we give the model a task with no prior examples. The model must rely only on its training knowledge.
It works well for common tasks, but the answer may vary in style or detail.
We use zero-shot when we do not have a clear pattern to demonstrate.

example.title: Zero-shot translation
example.content: Prompt: "Translate to French: I love coffee."

sections.heading: One-Shot Prompting
sections.subheading: Providing a single example before the task
paragraphs: One-shot prompting adds one example of the input and the expected output before the new question.
The single example helps the model see the format we expect.
It is useful when the task has a specific structure that the model might not guess on its own.

sections.heading: Few-Shot Prompting
sections.subheading: Showing several examples to guide the model
paragraphs: Few-shot prompting gives two or more examples, letting the model learn the pattern more clearly.
With several examples, the model’s responses become more consistent and follow the style we demonstrated.
This approach is helpful for tasks like classification, formatting, or creative writing.

example.title: Few-shot email classification
example.content: Prompt: "Email: 'Your package has shipped.' => Label: Shipping. Email: 'Your bill is due.' => Label: Billing. Email: 'We have a new offer for you.' => Label:"

sections.heading: Creating Your Own Few-Shot Prompt
sections.subheading: Step‑by‑step guide to building a prompt
paragraphs: 1. Choose a clear task (e.g., generate jokes).
2. Write 2‑3 short examples that show the input and the desired output.
3. Add a new question that follows the same pattern, leaving the answer blank for the model.
4. Keep the examples simple and consistent in style.

example.title: Few-shot joke generator
example.content: Prompt: "Q: Why did the chicken cross the road? A: To get to the other side. Q: Why is the math book sad? A: Because it has too many problems. Q: Why do programmers prefer dark mode? A:"

practice.title: Write a Few-Shot Prompt
practice.instruction: Create a prompt that asks the model to list three healthy snacks. First give two example snack‑name pairs, then add the new question for the model to answer.

keyTakeaways: Zero-shot prompting asks the model to perform a task without any examples.
One-shot prompting adds a single example to show the expected format.
Few-shot prompting provides several examples, making the model’s output more reliable and consistent.

mcqs.question: What does the term 'prompting' refer to in the context of language models?
options: Giving clear instructions to the model about the desired task
Training the model from scratch with new data
Storing user data for later use
mcqs.explanation: Prompting is the way we talk to a language model by writing a short text that tells it what we want it to do.

mcqs.question: Which statement best describes zero-shot prompting?
options: It provides two or more examples before the new question
It gives the model a task with no prior examples
It includes exactly one example to show the format
It uses only negative examples to guide the model
mcqs.explanation: Zero-shot prompting means we ask the model to perform a task without showing any examples, relying only on its existing knowledge.

mcqs.question: In the one-shot math example, what should the model answer after "Q: 5 + 3? A:"?
mcqs.explanation: The example shows the pattern "Q: 2 + 2? A: 4"; following the same format, 5 + 3 equals 8.

mcqs.question: According to the step‑by‑step guide, what is the first step when creating your own few-shot prompt?
options: Add a new question that follows the pattern
Keep the examples simple and consistent
mcqs.explanation: The guide lists the first step as choosing a clear task, such as generating jokes or listing snacks.

mcqs.question: Why does few-shot prompting often produce more reliable and consistent outputs?
options: It provides several examples that clarify the pattern we expect
It reduces the size of the language model
It removes the need for any training data
It forces the model to ignore its prior knowledge
mcqs.explanation: By showing two or more examples, few-shot prompting lets the model learn the desired format and style, leading to more consistent answers.
